finding: The distant center-left mountain gap is visible before the first blend after 236 opaque draws. Later fog/blend and snow passes do not create this particular gap. Root cause remains unresolved.

framebuffer.readback: GL4ES glReadPixels on rendering thread; GL error queue not consumed

later_interior_trace.scope: Native indexed depth-tested perspective draws and matrix/state snapshots. CPU projected triangle coverage is a diagnostic without depth, texture/shader or GPU equivalence; it is not a reference renderer.
later_interior_trace.candidate: At reduced framebuffer pixel (100,700), triangle indices 67/66/68 of captured draw 0055 cover the black interior gap. Mode TRIANGLES, count 168, UNSIGNED_INT; fog/blend enabled, culling disabled, LEQUAL with depth write. Inspect its full shader/texture/depth state next.
later_interior_trace.next: Make a minimal component reproduction with the captured triangle and exact native shaders; compare fog-enabled and fog-disabled output on a cleared target. Do not remove fog or alter game geometry as a workaround.

observations: Final native vertex/index inputs match the selected original triangle. Native MVP differs from double-precision CPU multiplication only by float rounding (maximum about 1.2e-7).
Readback before and after the original floor draw leaves pixel (200,1400), in top-left 2360x1640 coordinates, RGBA(0,0,0,0).
Repeating the original draw with depth disabled, or completing native GPU work before GL4ES frees scratch, does not fill that pixel.
A flat white diagnostic renders the triangle. Both textures with fog disabled give RGBA(42,44,31,255), lightmap only (128,167,166,255), detail only (84,67,48,255).

A later fog-only-disabled redraw gives the same textured pixel. Restoring fog and redrawing leaves that pixel unchanged; this does not yet establish whether the fog shader discarded coverage or reproduced that color.
Native fog uniforms and the three native fog coordinates are finite and match GL4ES state. Full unmodified scene still shows the gap after resuming.

limitations: Other empty regions in the base-pass image may simply await later draws.
Native frame readback adds synchronization; no performance claim.
One initial failed readback attempt may have retained a 15.48 MB debugger scratch allocation in this process.

No production source or guest memory was changed. Later diagnostic redraws temporarily changed GPU enable/current/texture/depth state under push/pop restoration; the final resumed scene still has the defect.
